text: "To what do you attribute your success?" And you can't say "luck". Because I think humble people will always say "luck" in some way, and I always kind of want to know, how self-aware are you, basically, and how curious are you?
speaker: Eeke De Miliano
context: Lenny is featuring favorite interview questions from previous podcast guests. Eeke De Miliano, former head of product at Retool and PM at Stripe, shares her go-to interview question for candidates. She explains that this question is designed to test self-awareness and curiosity, as it forces candidates to think deeply about their career journey rather than giving modest responses about luck.
text_ko: “자신의 성공을 무엇 덕분이라고 보세요?” 그리고 ‘운’이라고 대답하면 안 돼요. 겸손한 사람들은 흔히 그렇게 말하니까요. 저는 본질적으로 그 사람이 자기 인식(self-awareness)이 어느 정도인지, 그리고 호기심(curiosity)은 얼마나 강한지가 궁금해요.
text_zh: 你觉得自己的成功靠什么？别说“运气”。谦虚的人总会这么回答。我更想知道的是，你有多了解自己？你到底有多好奇？
text_es: ¿A qué atribuye usted su éxito? No puede decir "suerte". Creo que la gente humilde suele achacarlo a la "suerte" de alguna manera, y a mí siempre me interesa saber, básicamente, qué tan consciente es usted de sí mismo y qué tan curioso es.
key_sentence: You can't attribute your success to luck; self-awareness matters.
original_text: "To what do you attribute your success?" And you can't say "luck". Because I think humble people will always say "luck" in some way, and I always kind of want to know, how self-aware are you, basically, and how curious are you? I think people have really sort of gone back and reflected on why are they where they are today really says a lot about how they think about the world.

vocabulary.definition: To regard something as being caused by someone or something; to ascribe a quality or characteristic to a person or thing.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'attribute' is often used to identify the factors contributing to success, performance metrics, or customer satisfaction.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'attribute' can imply a positive recognition, it may also suggest a lack of personal responsibility if overused.

vocabulary.definition: Having a conscious knowledge of one's own character, feelings, motives, and desires.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, self-aware individuals are often seen as effective leaders who understand their strengths and weaknesses, leading to better decision-making and team dynamics.
vocabulary.nuance: Self-awareness is generally viewed positively, but excessive self-awareness can lead to overthinking or hesitation.

vocabulary.definition: Eager to know or learn something; inquisitive.
vocabulary.businessContext: Curiosity in business fosters innovation and problem-solving, as employees who are curious are more likely to explore new ideas and challenge the status quo.
vocabulary.nuance: While curiosity is typically a positive trait, it can be perceived negatively if it leads to prying into others' affairs or if it distracts from tasks.

vocabulary.definition: Having or showing a modest or low estimate of one's own importance; not arrogant.
vocabulary.businessContext: Humble leaders often create a positive workplace culture by valuing team contributions and fostering collaboration, which can enhance employee morale and productivity.
vocabulary.nuance: While humility is generally admired, excessive humility can sometimes be mistaken for a lack of confidence or assertiveness.

text: I ask, "What's the hardest thing you've ever done?" I ask that because working at Ramp is hard, and I want to understand what hard means for them. I want to understand why it was hard.
speaker: Geoff Charles
context: Geoff Charles, Head of Product at Ramp, explains his favorite interview question when Lenny asks about effective ways to evaluate candidates. This question helps him assess a candidate's resilience and problem-solving abilities, which are crucial for success at Ramp since the work environment is particularly challenging and demanding.
text_ko: 제가 "지금까지 해본 것 중 가장 힘들었던 건 뭐예요?"라고 물어봐요. Ramp에서 일하는 건 쉽지 않아서요, 그분들에게 '힘들다'가 무엇을 의미하는지, 또 왜 그 일이 힘들었는지 이해하고 싶어서요.
text_zh: 我会问：“你做过最难的一件事是什么？” 我这么问是因为在Ramp工作很不容易，我想知道对他们来说“难”是什么意思，也想弄清楚那件事为什么会那么难。
text_es: Les pregunto: «¿Qué es lo más difícil que han hecho?» Lo hago porque trabajar en Ramp es duro y quiero entender qué significa "duro" para cada persona; quiero saber por qué les resultó difícil.
key_sentence: I want to understand what hard means for them.
original_text: I ask, "What's the hardest thing you've ever done?" I ask that because working at Ramp is hard, and I want to understand what hard means for them. I want to understand why it was hard. I want to understand how they overcame that difficulty, how they worked with other people to overcome that difficulty, and how much agency they had in overcoming that.

vocabulary.definition: To grasp the meaning, significance, or nature of something; to comprehend fully.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding is crucial for effective communication, collaboration, and decision-making, as it allows stakeholders to align their goals and strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: Understanding implies a deeper level of insight beyond mere knowledge, often involving empathy and the ability to see things from others' perspectives.

text: Interestingly, all of a sudden the sharp product managers, engineers, basically every role, they very quickly find what are the one or two Eigenquestions on this topic.
speaker: Shishir Mehrotra
context: Shishir Mehrotra, CEO of Coda, describes his teleportation device interview question where candidates must identify the most important questions to ask. An "Eigenquestion" in his framework refers to the fundamental questions that unlock the most critical information needed to make strategic decisions. He explains how strong candidates quickly identify these core questions that drive all other business decisions.
text_ko: 흥미롭게도, 갑자기 유능한 프로덕트 매니저(PM)들, 엔지니어들, 사실상 거의 모든 역할의 사람들이 이 주제에 대해 한두 가지 핵심 질문(Eigenquestions)을 금세 찾아내요.
text_zh: 有意思的是，突然之间，那些敏锐的产品经理、工程师，几乎每个岗位的人，都能很快抓住这个话题的一两个关键问题（Eigenquestions）。
text_es: Lo curioso es que, de repente, los responsables de producto (product managers) más perspicaces, los ingenieros y, en general, prácticamente todos los roles, identifican enseguida cuáles son una o dos preguntas clave (Eigenquestions) sobre ese tema.
key_sentence: Sharp product managers quickly find Eigenquestions on the topic.
original_text: Interestingly, all of a sudden the sharp product managers, engineers, basically every role, they very quickly find what are the one or two Eigenquestions on this topic. There's no right answer, but I'll tell you one of my favorite ones, because the product manager said, "Okay, if I had to ask two questions, the two questions I would ask, one, is it safe enough for humans or not?"

vocabulary.definition: Product managers are professionals responsible for guiding the development, launch, and ongoing improvement of a product, ensuring it meets customer needs and aligns with business goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, product managers act as the bridge between engineering, marketing, and sales teams, prioritizing features and managing the product lifecycle.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a strategic role that requires both technical knowledge and strong interpersonal skills, distinguishing them from other managerial positions.

vocabulary.definition: Engineers are professionals who apply scientific and mathematical principles to design, develop, and maintain structures, systems, and technologies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of technology and startups, engineers are crucial for building products, solving technical problems, and innovating new solutions to meet market demands.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can refer to various specializations, such as software engineers or mechanical engineers, and is often associated with technical expertise and problem-solving capabilities.

text: The thought experiment for me is always, coming out of that, do I feel compelled to work on that problem? Right? No matter how boring it sounds on the surface, I think a really great product manager kind of casts something.
speaker: Yuhki Yamashita
context: Yuhki Yamashita, Chief Product Officer at Figma, discusses what he looks for when candidates describe big problems they've worked on. He explains that exceptional product managers have the ability to make any problem sound compelling and important through their storytelling skills, which is crucial since much of a PM's job involves communication and inspiring teams to work on challenging problems.
text_ko: 저는 늘 사고 실험(thought experiment)을 해요. 그걸 통해 '이 문제를 해결하는 일에 끌려서 직접 뛰어들고 싶다'는 마음이 드는지를 확인해요. 겉으로 아무리 지루해 보여도, 정말 훌륭한 제품 매니저(product manager)는 사람들을 끌어들이는 무언가를 만들어내요.
text_zh: 我通常的思考方式是这样的：从那点出发，我会问自己——我有没有一种非做不可的冲动去解决这个问题？对吧？不管表面上看起来多无聊，我觉得真正优秀的产品经理(product manager)总能把它讲成一个有吸引力的故事。
text_es: Mi experimento mental siempre es: cuando salgo de eso, ¿me dan ganas de ponerme a trabajar en ese problema? Por muy aburrido que parezca a primera vista, creo que un gran responsable de producto (product manager) de algún modo le da sentido.
key_sentence: A great product manager compels you to work on the problem.
original_text: The thought experiment for me is always, coming out of that, do I feel compelled to work on that problem? Right? No matter how boring it sounds on the surface, I think a really great product manager kind of casts something. It's like, "Well, this is why it's so existential and this is why it's so interesting, and really rallied the troops up.

vocabulary.definition: To be driven or forced to take a particular action or make a decision.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, being compelled often refers to a strong motivation to address a specific challenge or opportunity, indicating a sense of urgency or necessity.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'compelled' suggests a strong internal drive, it can also imply a lack of choice, so it should be used carefully to avoid connotations of coercion.

vocabulary.definition: To project or present an idea, image, or impression to others.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'casts' often refers to how leaders or managers communicate their vision or influence the perception of a product or brand among stakeholders.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a deliberate effort to shape perceptions, so it is best used in contexts where intention and impact are clear.

vocabulary.definition: A professional responsible for the strategy, roadmap, and feature definition of a product or product line.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, product managers play a crucial role in guiding cross-functional teams to develop products that meet market needs and align with business goals.
vocabulary.nuance: The role of a product manager can vary significantly across organizations, so it's important to clarify the specific responsibilities and authority associated with the title in different contexts.

text: Good answers are people who put structure and a way forward through the ambiguity. That's what you look for. You want your PM to not just be like, "Oh no, we're swimming in ambiguity," but actually put a path forward.
speaker: Jiaona Zhang
context: JZ, Head of Product at Webflow, explains her approach to behavioral interview questions when Lenny asks about evaluating PM candidates. She emphasizes that product management is inherently ambiguous, so she tests how candidates navigate unclear situations. The best candidates don't get paralyzed by uncertainty but instead create structure and actionable plans to move forward.
text_ko: 좋은 답을 주는 사람은 애매한 상황에서도 구조를 세우고 앞으로 나아갈 길을 제시하는 사람이에요. 그게 바로 당신이 찾는 사람이고요. 프로덕트 매니저(PM)가 그냥 "아, 불확실성 속에서 허우적대고 있다"만 말하는 사람이 아니라 실제로 갈 길을 만들어 주길 원해요.
text_zh: 好的回答是那些能在不确定性中理出头绪、找到前进方向的人。这就是你要找的。你希望你的产品经理(PM)不是那种遇到模糊情况就说"完了，咱们现在一头雾水"，而是能实实在在地规划出一条路来。
text_es: Las buenas respuestas vienen de gente que logra poner estructura y trazar un camino claro en medio de toda esa incertidumbre. Eso es lo que buscas. Quieres que tu PM no se quede ahí diciendo "Ay, no, estamos perdidos en la ambigüedad," sino que realmente proponga un plan para seguir adelante.
key_sentence: Good answers put structure through ambiguity and a path forward.

vocabulary.definition: The arrangement or organization of components within a system or framework.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, structure often refers to the organizational hierarchy or the systematic approach to project management that facilitates decision-making and efficiency.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'structure' implies order and clarity, it can also suggest rigidity, so it's important to balance structure with flexibility.

vocabulary.definition: The quality of being open to more than one interpretation; uncertainty or inexactness.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, ambiguity can arise in project requirements, market conditions, or stakeholder expectations, necessitating clear communication and strategic planning.
vocabulary.nuance: Ambiguity often carries a negative connotation in business, as it can lead to confusion and indecision, but it can also indicate complexity that requires careful navigation.

vocabulary.definition: A strategic plan or course of action designed to achieve a specific goal or overcome challenges.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, a 'path forward' is often proposed to address obstacles or to capitalize on opportunities, guiding teams toward actionable steps.
vocabulary.nuance: The phrase suggests a proactive and solution-oriented mindset, emphasizing the importance of moving beyond problems rather than dwelling on them.

text: "What unfair secrets have you learned to improve the velocity and energy level of a product team?" When I say "unfair" or "secret", I usually mean not something that you probably read on a media. "What did you learn? How did you learn it?
speaker: Noah Weiss
context: Noah Weiss, Chief Product Officer at Slack, shares his favorite interview question when Lenny asks about creative ways to evaluate candidates. He's looking for unique insights or unconventional methods that candidates have discovered through experience rather than from commonly available resources like blog posts or articles. This helps him identify people with genuine hands-on learning and innovative thinking.
text_ko: 프로덕트 팀(product team)의 속도(velocity)와 에너지 레벨(energy level)을 높이기 위해 터득한, 남들이 잘 모르는 '불공정한 비결'이 있나요? 제가 'unfair'나 'secret'이라고 말할 때는 보통 미디어에서 볼 수 있는 평범한 조언이 아니라 공개적으로 잘 알려지지 않은 실전 팁을 뜻해요. 무엇을 배웠고, 그걸 어떻게 배웠나요?
text_zh: 你学到过哪些能显著提升产品团队推进速度(velocity)和士气(energy level)的“不公平”的秘诀？当我说“unfair”或“secret”时，我指的不是那些你在媒体上随处能看到的公开做法。你具体学到了什么？又是怎么学到的？
text_es: ¿Qué secretos “injustos” has aprendido para mejorar la velocidad (velocity) y el nivel de energía (energy level) de un equipo de producto? Cuando digo “injusto” o “secreto” me refiero a cosas que probablemente no encontrarás en los medios. ¿Qué aprendiste y cómo lo aprendiste?
key_sentence: Unfair secrets improve the velocity and energy level of a product team.
original_text: "What unfair secrets have you learned to improve the velocity and energy level of a product team?" When I say "unfair" or "secret", I usually mean not something that you probably read on a media. "What did you learn? How did you learn it? How does it work, and how do you apply it?"

vocabulary.definition: Velocity refers to the speed of something in a given direction, often used to describe the rate of progress or movement in a specific context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, velocity is frequently used to measure the speed at which a team delivers work or a product reaches the market, particularly in agile methodologies.
vocabulary.nuance: While velocity implies speed, it also suggests efficiency and effectiveness in achieving goals, making it a critical metric in performance assessments.

vocabulary.definition: Energy level refers to the amount of vitality or enthusiasm exhibited by individuals or teams, influencing their productivity and engagement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, maintaining high energy levels within teams is crucial for fostering creativity, collaboration, and overall performance, especially in fast-paced environments.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often carries a positive connotation, suggesting motivation and dynamism, and is typically used in discussions about team morale and workplace culture.

text: "What's something that everyone takes for granted that you think is essentially hogwash or inaccurate?" Sometimes I'll ask a manager, "Look, you've managed hundreds of people in your career. What's conventional wisdom that you bet against, that you have found is actually inaccurate?"
speaker: Nikhyl Singhal
context: Nikhyl Singhal, VP of Product at Facebook, explains his strategy for breaking through typical interview responses when Lenny asks about authentic ways to evaluate candidates. This question forces people to share genuine opinions and challenge widely accepted beliefs, helping him assess whether candidates can think independently and avoid giving rehearsed answers that don't reveal their true thinking.
text_ko: 사람들이 다들 당연하게 여기는 것 중에 사실 본질적으로 엉터리이거나 틀렸다고 생각하는 게 뭐예요? 가끔 매니저들에게 이렇게 물어봐요. "경력 동안 수백 명을 관리해오셨잖아요. 사람들이 당연하게 믿는 통념(conventional wisdom) 중에서 당신이 반대했던, 그리고 실제로는 틀렸다고 확인된 게 뭐예요?"
text_zh: "有什么事情是大家都觉得理所当然，但你认为其实是胡扯或者不对的？"有时候我会问管理者："你看，你职业生涯中管过几百号人了，有什么所谓的传统观念(conventional wisdom)是你不认同的，觉得其实是错的？"
text_es: "¿Hay algo que todo el mundo da por sentado pero que tú consideras puras tonterías o incorrecto?" A veces le pregunto a un gerente: "Mira, has dirigido a cientos de personas en tu carrera. ¿Qué sabiduría convencional rechazas, que has comprobado que en realidad está equivocada?"
key_sentence: Conventional wisdom often takes for granted what is essentially hogwash.

vocabulary.definition: Conventional wisdom refers to widely accepted beliefs or opinions that are generally taken for granted as true or valid.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, conventional wisdom can influence decision-making and strategic planning, often leading organizations to follow established norms without questioning their validity.
vocabulary.nuance: While conventional wisdom can provide a useful framework, it may also stifle innovation if not critically examined.

vocabulary.definition: To bet against means to take a position that something will fail or underperform, often in a financial context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In investment and trading, betting against a stock or market trend indicates a belief that the asset's value will decrease, which can be a high-risk strategy.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase carries a connotation of skepticism and can imply a contrarian viewpoint, which may not always be well-received.

vocabulary.definition: Essentially means fundamentally or in essence, highlighting the core nature or most important aspect of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communication, using 'essentially' can help clarify complex ideas by distilling them to their most important points, making discussions more efficient.
vocabulary.nuance: This term can sometimes imply simplification, so it should be used carefully to avoid oversimplifying complex issues.
